wy_downpour_wall.blurb: Downpour Wall is a steep, pocketed face in the Mondo Beyondo sector near the top of Ten Sleep Canyon. All 29 routes are bolted sport lines, and the wall is a good pick for stronger climbers: the bulk sit in the 5.12 range, with a decent handful of 5.11 and 5.13 routes, a few 5.10s, and just one easier line near 5.7. The wall faces south, yet at roughly 7,700 feet it holds up reasonably cool through the year. Expect a steady uphill walk from the road to reach the base.

wy_south_and_east_faces.blurb: These two sides of Devils Tower hold the tower's busiest crack climbs. Most of the 28 routes are traditional lines, with a few aid pitches and a couple of bolted sport routes mixed in. Typical routes take two long pitches to reach the meadows on the summit plateau, and the grades stretch from about 5.6 to the low 5.12s, clustering around 5.9 to 5.12. The cracks run mostly straight up and down, so a double rack of cams and nuts is the usual choice. Some of the slabby approach rock is slick underfoot, which matters when carrying a heavy pack.

wy_erratic_the.blurb: The Erratic is a sector on the back side of Wild Iris, southwest of Lander. It has 28 routes, nearly all of them sport climbs plus a single boulder problem. The wall is a clean, pale face, steep in its first section, with pocket pulling throughout. It stays mostly shady, which helps on warm days, though summer weekends bring plenty of company. Routes begin around 5.10 and are mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with a smaller group of 5.13 and harder lines for those who want a project, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steep rock.

wy_east_and_northeast_buttress_approach.blurb: This section of Devils Tower covers the east and northeast sides, where straight-in crack climbing runs from offwidths down to fingers. Of the 28 routes, most are trad, with a few aid, sport and top-rope options. Grades run from an easy scramble-level pitch up into the 5.12s, with the greatest number between 5.10 and 5.12. A big roof system cuts across the sheer east face, and a prominent buttress juts out partway up the tower. The trail in is faint in places and passes through poison ivy, so long pants help.

wy_white_heat_wall.blurb: White Heat Wall is a clean panel of limestone in the western part of Sinks Canyon, just outside Lander. It sits right of Addiction Wall and joins up with Brisket Wall. All 27 routes are bolted sport lines, running from about 5.9 up to 5.14, with the weight in the 5.11 and 5.12 grades and a good handful of 5.13s. There is little here for beginners, and few warm-ups, but it is a solid stop for intermediate-to-hard sport climbers. The wall picks up sun through the afternoon, so plan around the heat or the cold.

wy_purple_galaxy.blurb: Purple Galaxy is a sport wall toward the left end of the main cliff line in Sinks Canyon, near Lander. The 27 routes are all bolted, and the grade range is tight: everything falls between 5.10 and 5.13, with the bulk at 5.11 and 5.12. Several lines are long, running past 25 metres, so a rope of ample length is worth bringing. The wall carries fewer routes than the neighbouring crags, which can mean more elbow room, and it is a good fit for climbers who already lead 5.10 and want sustained pitches.
